description: Reviewed Ultron A01-A46 acceptance instrument. Evidence tests are matched by name substring against vitest JSON results (fullName). Change only through a recorded review, then run npm run acceptance:lock.

rows.behavior: Direct/graph/RLM invocation shares one definition and result contract

tests: runs an explicit background job through the same durable task host
runs deterministic agents and preserves durable task records

rows.notes: Background and agent dispatch share the durable task host. No parity suite compares direct, workflow-graph, and RLM invocation of the same definition and result contract.

rows.behavior: Large input stays outside active context; full data remains usable
rows.notes: No evidence: no large-data fixture capturing request sizes against expected output.

rows.behavior: Invalid result triggers bounded repair or typed failure

tests: rejects malformed reviewer output instead of claiming success
only a completed prompt at its returned tip can succeed
rejects malformed schemas and executable payload values

rows.notes: Typed failure on invalid output is tested. Bounded repair (maxRepairs > 0) with a semantically invalid result is not exercised.

rows.behavior: Root pin and explicit child model are preserved

tests: invoke through the real host keeps the child's model and tools and links the parent

rows.notes: Child model preservation is tested for skill invocation only. Root pin capture and the live provider smoke require a metered live run (not part of this deterministic report).

rows.behavior: Cancellation terminates owned work and rejects late success

tests: cancellation commits a terminal result without waiting for a stuck lane
parent cancellation before admission does not start a task
timeout has a bounded range and commits cancellation
queued cancellation leaves the active cell running
active cancellation stops Python and propagates to host work
returns the committed terminal record when completion races cancellation

rows.notes: Cancellation and late-success races are covered for lanes and the kernel. A real external process-tree fixture is missing.

rows.behavior: Output, artifact, wall-time, concurrency, and process limits hold

tests: rejects oversized input without losing existing Python state
rejects malformed protocol and startup stalls
timeout has a bounded range and commits cancellation

rows.notes: Input and wall-time bounds only. No flooding/hanging worker matrix for output, artifact, concurrency, and process limits.

rows.behavior: Branch/fork/resume restores matching state; no abandoned lesson leak

tests: uses the real JsonlSessionRepo and scopes discovery to cwd
resolves exact ids, unique prefixes, and rejects ambiguous prefixes
continue selects by modification time, not creation time
recovers unfinished tasks as interrupted and persists the recovery

rows.notes: Session selection and task recovery only. No branch/fork/resume state-restoration or abandoned-lesson leak test across restart.

rows.behavior: Unsupported Python state reports non-restorable, never silently correct
rows.notes: No evidence: no snapshot type matrix or tamper rejection test for Python kernel state.

rows.behavior: Concurrent calls/retries cannot bypass tree budget admission

tests: concurrent idempotent invokes share the same live promise
uses one durable document and detects idempotency conflicts
admission failure from the usage budget is recorded once per slot without a retry storm

rows.notes: Idempotent concurrent invokes and one budget-admission failure path. No nested tree-budget race matrix, missing-usage, or unknown-pricing fixtures.

rows.behavior: Worker receives no ambient credentials or unauthorized host capability

tests: model-written Python sees no ambient credentials or worker control channel
explicit allow-list passes a named variable through
dispatches by prefix and passes the calling task from the lane, not the payload

rows.notes: Trusted-local profile only: environment inspection inside the real kernel and capability denial through host requests. Not a hostile-code isolation claim.

rows.behavior: Approval binds scope/revision/policy and is rechecked
rows.notes: No evidence: approval scope/revision/policy binding is not implemented in the default native path.

rows.behavior: Graph validates before effects; routes/skips/fan-in/cycles are explicit

tests: validates every workflow node, normalizes missing dependencies, and skips failed dependencies

rows.notes: Validation-before-effects and cycle rejection are tested. Routes, fan-in, and explicit skip records lack a contract suite.

rows.behavior: Agent admission does not satisfy a graph dependency
rows.notes: No evidence: no slow-child fixture with a delayed valid result proving admission does not satisfy a dependency.

rows.behavior: No checks/incomplete review/stale receipt cannot imply verified completion

tests: rejects malformed reviewer output instead of claiming success
runs an explicit background job through the same durable task host
never verifies a completion claim without a passing verifier
required gate: achieved only when every required check succeeds with passed === true

rows.notes: No-check and failed-check paths stay unverified. Stale receipt and incomplete-review fixtures are missing.

rows.behavior: Baseline versus candidate is recorded; required regressions block
rows.notes: No evidence: no baseline/candidate checker with protected inputs.

rows.behavior: Memory skip causes no retrieval; scopes survive consolidation

tests: requires Jev and concrete scope tags, and a skipped recall does not call the backend
sends exact tags and refuses recalled documents outside the requested scope

rows.notes: Skip-means-no-retrieval and scope tags are tested against a fake backend. Scope survival through consolidation and a real backend contract are missing.

rows.behavior: Correction supersedes stale claims; hypotheses remain distinguishable
rows.notes: No evidence: memory correct() API exists but no contradictory-claim scenario across fresh sessions.

rows.behavior: Ingestion acceptance is distinct from completed retention; forgetting persists

tests: does not claim an async write is stored until a receipt completes
an interrupted backend mutation becomes unknown and cannot be edited or replayed

rows.notes: Acceptance versus completed retention is tested. Forgetting persistence across backend restart is missing.

rows.behavior: Refiner cannot alter policy, grants, or acceptance tests

tests: rejects path-like and protected refinement targets without touching documents

rows.notes: Protected-target rejection only. Capability-escalation and policy/grant edit proposals are not exercised.

rows.behavior: Versioned refinement changes later behavior and can roll back

tests: requires evidence, validates activation, and preserves rollback history
stores refinements through injected documents and enforces versions without approval

rows.notes: Versioning and rollback bookkeeping are tested. No before/after/rollback task proving changed later behavior.

rows.behavior: Replay does not duplicate external effects; uncertainty stays explicit

tests: an interrupted backend mutation becomes unknown and cannot be edited or replayed
a restart on the same stores does not re-run a completed or claimed slot

rows.notes: Uncertain mutations stay explicit and schedule slots are not replayed. No lost-response external-effect service fixture.

rows.behavior: Detached work and retained children survive UI loss
rows.notes: No evidence: no real supervisor/client disconnect and reconnect test with retained children.

rows.behavior: Schedules/goals/verification compose within budgets

tests: duplicate and concurrent ticks in the same slot run the slot once
a restart on the same stores does not re-run a completed or claimed slot
missed ticks coalesce into one run for the latest slot and record the skipped count
max_runs completes a schedule and pause stops firings
a paused goal stops attached schedule firings and resume re-enables them
required gate: achieved only when every required check succeeds with passed === true
max_tasks caps schedule firings, verification, and attachments
admission failure from the usage budget is recorded once per slot without a retry storm
the background timer fires due slots and stops on close
rejects unknown payload fields and forged identity

rows.notes: Dedicated A23 suite: duplicate, missed, and restart ticks, goal pause, required gate, and budget admission.

rows.behavior: Costs, task transitions, and inspection agree on one record
rows.notes: No evidence: no event reconstruction or accounting reconciliation test tying costs, transitions, and inspection to one record.

rows.behavior: Existing Pi capabilities and data survive migration and rollback

tests: reconstructs Pi turn and agent boundaries from lane events
runs prompts, bash, and session commands through the native worker

rows.notes: RPC compatibility only. No profile parity, import/export, or backup restoration rehearsal.

rows.behavior: Component changes cannot pass merely by weakening tests
rows.notes: Evidence is this instrument: acceptance/instrument.lock (checked by the report) and the mutation slice in acceptance/mutation.json. Independent human review of the instrument is a process step, not automated, so the row cannot pass automatically.

rows.behavior: RLM handles a self-contained task without graph/delegation/memory/refinement

tests: preserves Python state and returns host replies and Python errors
keeps Python state across tool invocations and exposes protocol errors

rows.notes: Kernel runs without optional services. No test asserts a self-contained task completes with zero graph, delegation, memory, or refinement dispatches.

rows.behavior: Retrieval explanation/query/scope match the executed search; rewrite cannot widen access

tests: sends exact tags and refuses recalled documents outside the requested scope
why shows the evidence that was injected, with no new search and no other task's scope

rows.notes: Scope enforcement on recall. No query rewrite failure or rewrite-widening test.

rows.behavior: Memory inspector shows actual injected evidence without a new search or hidden-scope disclosure

tests: why shows the evidence that was injected, with no new search and no other task's scope
the inspector refuses requests that would search or change state

rows.notes: Dedicated A29 suite with a fake backend: no new search, no cross-task scope leak, inspection-only requests.

rows.behavior: Correction/deletion propagates to managed memory views/exports without changing trusted instructions
rows.notes: No evidence: no export/cache propagation or AGENTS.md preservation test for correction/deletion.

rows.behavior: Skill selection is version-pinned, explainable, and cannot grant capabilities

tests: lists skills with content-hash versions and invocability
select explains each candidate, ranks deterministically, and records the decision
why returns the original decision after the catalog changes
version-pinned load succeeds and a stale version is rejected
capability-granting frontmatter is reported and never reaches the spawned child
invoke through the real host keeps the child's model and tools and links the parent
concurrent loads, selects, and invokes each observe one catalog snapshot while content changes
disableModelInvocation skills are listed but cannot be invoked
rejects unknown payload fields, forged identity, and malformed arguments
durable state survives a new module instance and records catalog changes across restarts

rows.notes: Dedicated A31 suite: pinned versions, explanations, capability non-grant, concurrent activation.

rows.behavior: Skill proposals require evidence, validation, and applicable approval; rejection/rollback holds

tests: requires evidence, validates activation, and preserves rollback history
stores refinements through injected documents and enforces versions without approval

rows.notes: Evidence, validation, and rollback for refinements. Applicable approval is disabled and repeated-procedure/duplicate skill proposal cases are missing.

rows.behavior: Experiment history includes all attempts and variants do not contaminate each other

tests: records and compares only matched experiment fixtures

rows.notes: Matched-fixture recording only. No memory/skill isolation between variants or failed-run usage reconciliation.

rows.behavior: Optional-service failure preserves RLM operation without bypassing required checks or replaying effects

tests: requires Jev and concrete scope tags, and a skipped recall does not call the backend
does not dispatch when already aborted and redacts fetch failures
rejects invalid probabilities instead of clamping or defaulting

rows.notes: Jev/memory fail closed. No combined outage run showing RLM continues without bypassing required checks.

rows.behavior: Deterministic/predict/rlm methods share policy, validation, accounting, and task semantics

tests: runs deterministic agents and preserves durable task records
requires adapters for predict and non-identity deterministic definitions

rows.notes: Deterministic path and adapter requirements. No strategy parity test for accounting or that predict launches no kernel.

rows.behavior: Invocation scratch is isolated while declared instance state persists
rows.notes: No evidence: retained-instance state versus invocation scratch is not exposed or tested.

rows.behavior: Bounded preview preserves full values and does not execute unsafe introspection on the host

tests: deduplicates and reads artifacts with integrity and range checks

rows.notes: Artifact range reads only. No large-value, cyclic, or hostile-repr preview test in this suite.

rows.behavior: Nested context excludes unauthorized and contaminating history
rows.notes: No evidence: no captured reviewer request or scope-restricted event query test.

rows.behavior: Configured models can use the actual typed RLM interface
rows.notes: Requires the metered live capability suite (npm run eval:capabilities) with repeated trials; not run by this deterministic report.

rows.behavior: Retained instances accept new invocations without rewriting old terminal outcomes

tests: reopened invoke returns the durable result, not undefined
enforces forward transitions and matching terminal results

rows.notes: Terminal records are immutable. Retained-instance follow-up invocations are not exposed.

rows.behavior: Family messages enforce identity, scope, deduplication, expiry, and safe delivery

tests: rejects forged sender fields and takes the sender from the calling lane
delivers between parent and child in both directions, including root
rejects siblings, grandchildren, and other families
replays a keyed send idempotently and rejects conflicting content under the same key
never delivers expired messages and reports them as expired
rejects sends to a full inbox and oversized messages instead of dropping
receive is at-most-once and respects limit and FIFO order
steers a live receiver through the host and falls back to the inbox otherwise
isolates verifiers to their direct parent and never steers them
validates payloads strictly
durable state survives a new module instance on the same store
serializes concurrent sends against the inbox cap
derives identity from real task lanes and steers a live child lane

rows.notes: Dedicated A41 suite: forged sender, cross-family, saturation, replay, expiry, steering, verifier isolation.

rows.behavior: Human child intervention and subtree stop preserve unrelated work

tests: cancellation commits a terminal result without waiting for a stuck lane

rows.notes: Single-child cancellation only. No two-child inspect/correct/stop run proving unrelated work continues.

rows.behavior: Resource release/eviction respects live references, evidence retention, and quotas
rows.notes: No evidence: no pinned checkpoint, live artifact, idle eviction, or quota test.

rows.behavior: Progress and reassessment use evidence and cannot extend budgets or declare unsupported success

tests: classifies stalled, progressing, busy, and finished from recorded evidence
takes the reporter from the lane and rejects reports for unrelated tasks
validates payloads strictly and bounds evidence and receipts
always denies budget extension and records the reason
never verifies a completion claim without a passing verifier
persists receipts and decisions across module instances and settles interrupted verifications
rejects a corrupt stored document

rows.notes: Dedicated A44 suite: stalled/busy/progressing fixtures, budget-extension denial, unknown-verifier cases.

rows.behavior: Saturated nested recursion makes progress or returns bounded capacity failure, never deadlock
rows.notes: No evidence: no parent-awaiting-child saturation or bounded capacity failure test.

rows.behavior: The combined system performs the full demonstration without manual state repair
rows.notes: Combined fix/review/retain/refine demonstration is not implemented; also needs a live RLM run plus deterministic failure variants.
